title: Reading list
html:
All links were opened on the day they were added.

Courses and books

  • Google, Machine Learning Crash Course: free, practical, with exercises.
  • James, Witten, Hastie and Tibshirani, An Introduction to Statistical Learning: free book with video lectures; the best bridge between statistics and machine learning.
  • Deisenroth, Faisal and Ong, Mathematics for Machine Learning: free book.
  • Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning: free, the reference for neural networks.
  • Stanford CS229 lecture notes: Ng's rigorous course, for when you want the maths.

Practical guides

  • Google, Rules of Machine Learning: best practices from engineers.
  • Domingos, A Few Useful Things to Know about Machine Learning: twelve lessons in a dozen pages.
  • The scikit-learn user guide, especially model evaluation, cross-validation, preprocessing and calibration, and the algorithm cheat sheet.
  • The NumPy quickstart.

Maths

  • Khan Academy: statistics and probability, linear algebra, calculus.
  • Brown University, Seeing Theory: probability and statistics, interactive.
  • 3Blue1Brown, neural network series and dot products.

Neural networks

  • Andrej Karpathy, Neural Networks: Zero to Hero: build up to a GPT, in code.
  • Keras, The Sequential model and the Dense layer: the library calls used in section 14.5.
  • Grinsztajn et al., Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on tabular data?

LLMs, agents and retrieval

  • Anthropic, Building effective agents and Contextual Retrieval.
  • Anthropic documentation: tool use overview and Handle tool calls.
  • Yao et al., ReAct; Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
  • sentence-transformers for local embeddings; sqlglot for parsing SQL.
